problemStatement.formal: For finite 3-uniform hypergraphs G, study the families F_G(kappa) of 3-uniform hypergraphs with chromatic number kappa avoiding G; are the bounded-witness, intersection, and uncountable-cardinal transfer conjectures true?
problemStatement.plain: Erdos #1177 asks three related questions about 3-uniform hypergraphs of uncountable chromatic number that avoid a fixed finite forbidden hypergraph.
whyMatters: The problem packages three Erdos-Galvin-Hajnal conjectures about forbidden subhypergraph families.
It tests whether high chromatic number can be transferred between uncountable cardinals while preserving forbidden-pattern avoidance.
The Lean file proves cardinal scaffolding from Mathlib but keeps the hypergraph primitives abstract.

proven: Mathlib proves the cardinal facts `aleph0_lt_aleph1`, `aleph1_uncountable`, and `aleph1_le_beth2`.
Lean defines `forbiddenFamily`, `forbiddenFamilyNonempty`, the three conjectures, and the combined statement `erdos_1177`.
Structural theorems prove simultaneous nonemptiness from Conjecture 3, the identical-forbidden-graph case of Conjecture 2, and anti-monotonicity of forbidden families.
open: Conjecture1, Conjecture2, and Conjecture3 are definitions and are not proved in this file.
The 3-uniform hypergraph type, vertex cardinality, subgraph containment, finiteness, and chromatic number are active axioms.
`erdos_1177` is only the conjunction of the three conjectures, not a theorem.
knownResults.goal: Keep the proved cardinal/structural lemmas separate from the abstract hypergraph interface and the three open conjectures.

currentState.focus: Metadata now describes the three forbidden-hypergraph conjectures, the proved Mathlib cardinal facts, and the five active Hypergraph3 axioms.
blockers: Hypergraph3 is represented by five abstract axioms.
The three Erdos-Galvin-Hajnal conjectures remain unproved.
currentState.nextAction: A useful proof slice would replace part of the abstract Hypergraph3 interface with concrete definitions or prove more relations between the three conjectures.
